text:
jamie: heads-up — on the long-context perf job I see steady RSS growth even after requests finish. suspect KV cache fragmentation rather than leak.

sasha: can you paste the profiler snapshot? rough numbers are fine.

jamie: pasted below — this is after a 2h run with many >32k token sessions:
```
# top sections
rss: 42.6GB -> 46.1GB over 2h
malloced: 38.9GB
free_segments: 12% (mostly small holes)
avg_alloc_block: 4KB
num_blocks: 9.7M
compaction_count: 0
last_eviction_ms: 8ms
```

pat: 12% free segments sounds like fragmentation to me. allocator seems to be handing out many small blocks. what block size/profile are you using?

jamie: default slab sizes (256B, 1KB, 4KB, 16KB). workload has lots of variable-length KV entries from attention heads, many short and a few large (>64KB) when long contexts appear.

ari: that's the classic mixed-size workload that breaks slab allocs — small items occupy slabs and big items get split across pages, causing holes. any correlation with eviction thresholds?

jamie: eviction only triggers on configured max_kv_mem per model. We hit eviction, but eviction doesn't compact adjacent freed segments — we end up with many tiny free chunks.

ben: fwiw, I ran a microbench: freeing 8K then allocating 48K causes fragmentation if allocator can't coalesce across slab-classes. coalescing policy matters.

jamie: timeline of observed regressions: after ~45m of sustained long sessions, tail latency P99 increases from 320ms to 760ms. correlates with RSS growth and increased background GC/alloc stalls.

pat: do we have a compaction prototype? I remember a background compactor that merges free ranges but it was disabled for perf reasons.

ari: we have two prototypes: 1) synchronous on-evict compaction (coalesce at eviction time) — immediate memory reduction but 5-20ms pause per compaction; 2) async background compactor that scans and defragments during idle cycles — low pause, but scheduling complexity.

jamie: ran quick A/B earlier today. sync compaction reduced RSS by ~3GB quickly but P99 spiked during compaction windows. async compactor kept P99 stable but needed tuned scan rate; after 2h it reclaimed only ~1.2GB.

ben: metrics from that run (timestamps relative):
```
run A (sync): reclaimed 3.1GB in 60s, avg compaction pause 12ms, p99 latency bump +220ms
run B (async): reclaimed 1.2GB over 2h, avg compaction work 0.8ms per cycle, p99 stable
```

sasha: tradeoff is clear: synchronous is effective but harmful to SLOs. async needs smarter heuristics to target high-value gaps. maybe prioritize coalescing hotspots near largest allocations?

pat: or adaptively switch modes: async most of the time, but trigger sync if free ratio > X and expected fragmentation will cause OOM/risk. we could bound compaction time to avoid >Y ms pause.

jamie: other idea — tune slab block sizes for mixed distributions. increase medium block class from 4KB->8KB reduced internal fragmentation in a sim by ~18% (but increased wasted space for many tiny entries).

ari: yep. We should gather real distribution histograms per model and auto-suggest slab profiles. Redwood Optimize could recommend per-model profiles.

ben: one more angle: avoid splitting large KV entries across many fragments — support large contiguous allocations backed by separate huge-page pool. reduces fragmentation churn when big contexts appear. huge pages also reduce TLB overhead.

sasha: sounds promising. risks: complexity in allocator and rare memory being reserved but unused. need telemetry to know when to enable.

jamie: proposed short-term plan:
1) enable async compactor with aggressive heuristics in staging for 24h (adaptive scan rate by RSS delta)
2) add a safeguard: if reclaimed <1GB in 1h and free segments>15% -> schedule bounded sync compaction capped at 30ms slots
3) collect fine-grained histograms of KV sizes per-model and run slab reconfig experiments nightly
4) prototype large-contig pool in dev, measure memory use and perf

pat: +1. add an opt-in flag for Dedicated customers to test huge-page pool.

ari: for the telemetry piece — please include: per-model histograms, compaction events (type,duration,reclaimed_bytes), eviction count, P50/P95/P99 latencies pre/post compaction.

jamie: will instrument and flip async compactor in staging now. posting results in ~24h.

infra-bot: deploy queued: async-compactor=on to staging at 1909990024 by jamie — rollout 5% pods -> 100% over 10m.

sasha: thanks. if you see p99 blips, revert and we can enable bounded sync only during low traffic windows. :thumbsup:

jamie: noted — will watch dashboards and dump another snapshot after the 24h run. cheers.
